HealthStatus.description:
Model health status — must stay in sync with the values
actually written by the LLM-models manager + Rust proxy
health probes. Missing a real status value here causes a
`fastapi.exceptions.ResponseValidationError` 500 when an
admin endpoint tries to serialize a model row whose
`health_status` column carries that value (the user's
"Failed to load deployments" with `degraded` was exactly
this pattern).

Source of truth in the LLM-models manager —
`app/services/llm/model/llm_models_manager.py`:
  * `healthy`         last probe passed
  * `unhealthy`       last probe failed
  * `degraded`        partial failure / intermittent — set by
                      the probe path when retries succeed but

RunAction.description:
One governed call inside a run — the leaf of the trajectory.

The unit the authorization plane has always called an *action*
(`action_type`); the ledger uses the same unit. Its ancestry travels

post.description:
Recomputes each row's hash and checks it against its stored value and its predecessor, reports sequence gaps, and validates any signed checkpoints covering the range.

Verdicts: `verified` (hashes link **and** a valid checkpoint covers them — the only verdict asserting integrity), `unattested` (hashes link, nothing signed them), `gap` (rows were deleted), `broken` (a hash does not match), `unchained` (rows predate the chain — not a pass and not a failure).

`truncated: true` means the scan stopped at the limit, so the verdict describes the range examined and not the whole chain. Requires the `system:read` permission.

        Tenant isolation:

        The deleted rows are declared in the audit chain's prune record

Stream every proxy log row that matches the filters as CSV or JSONL,
        with a self-describing metadata header. The body is the body of
        ``/query`` and every filter means what it means there, so the file
        holds the rows the list shows for the same filters. ``limit`` and
        ``offset`` page the list and are not used: the export is the whole
        matching set, in the order ``sort_by`` and ``sort_order`` give.

        Same tenant isolation rules as ``/query``:

        - Tenant admins are pinned to their tenant.
        - System admins must pass ``tenant_id``.

        Output format:
        - ``format=csv`` → ``text/csv``; metadata is emitted as ``# key: value``
          comment lines, followed by the column header and rows.
        - ``format=jsonl`` → ``application/x-ndjson``; first line is a
          ``{"_meta": {...}}`` envelope, then one JSON record per line.

        At most 50,000 rows: a larger matching set is refused with HTTP 413;
        narrow the filters.

        Body text, and the free-text filter ``q`` over it, need
        ``proxy:logs:read_bodies`` as they do in ``/query``.

        Changes nothing but the admin audit trail, where each export is
        recorded with its filters (``action = "export_proxy_logs"``).
